summary: Revision 2 (sha 070f0176...) resolves DES-1 to DES-4. Every requirement R1-R8 and AC1-AC11 maps to a component and an automated test. Contracts, data design, security controls and failure modes match the approved brief. No AI features.

criteria.description: Every requirement maps to a component and a test
criteria.notes: R1-R8 map to components. AC1-AC11 and NFR3 map to named test files and cases.

criteria.description: Schemas, errors, auth and limits are complete
criteria.notes: Note schema, error table, per-endpoint statuses, identity rules, size cap and check order match the brief.

criteria.description: Data design is sound and covers failure modes
criteria.notes: Map<user,Map<id,note>>, temp file plus fsync plus atomic rename, serialized queue with rollback, refusal to start on leftover tmp or corrupt file, 500-note cap.

criteria.description: Security design present and consistent with brief
criteria.notes: No TBD remains. Owner-only access with 404, X-User validation before body read, loopback bind, content-free logs, 0600 file.

criteria.description: Automated tests cover the acceptance criteria
criteria.notes: node:test matrix including __proto__ user, sentinel log test, forced 500, restart and corrupt-file tests.

findings.title: Logger scope vs 500 handler logging
findings.detail: The Logger takes only four fields, but the Security section says the 500 handler also logs the error class name and a request counter. The channel for that is unspecified. The 'exactly one line per request' test in AC10 could conflict.
findings.recommendation: At implementation, either add a separate fixed-field error log method or drop the extra line. Resolved when the logging test passes with a forced 500.

findings.title: Check order with Content-Length 413
findings.detail: Content-Type (415) is checked before the size check, as in the brief. Implementers should keep that order in the 413 fast path.
findings.recommendation: Cover with a test that sends an oversize body with a bad Content-Type and expects 415.

resolvedFindings.resolution: The sentence is gone. Deployment now says access is owner-only with 404 for non-owners, mapped to the AC3 and AC4 tests.
Security section is fully specified. No TBD remains.
Persistence, limits, error contract and the nested Map are all specified.
Automated test plan with an AC-to-test matrix.
